To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) mudflow events in Uzbekistan are mainly related to synoptic-scale atmospheric processes, which are associated with the advection of moist air masses from central Europe; (2) the frequency of mudflow events is higher during the advection period of moist air masses, which is associated with the advections of cyclonic (W, SW) and anticyclonic (C) stream flows from central Europe.
mudflows are more likely to occur when moist air from the west reaches Uzbekistan and the frequency of mudflow occurrence is higher when the air masses originate from the west, southwest and south.
the majority of mudflow events in Uzbekistan are related to the advection of moist air from Europe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for mudflow hazard assessment based on synoptic weather patterns.
the identification of the main synoptic weather types, which cause mudflows in the piedmont area of Uzbekistan.

the analysis of historical data on mudflow occurrences in central Asia and the application of the CWT method in order to understand the atmospheric factors, which are responsible for the interannual and longer-term variability in mudflow events.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
synoptic weather patterns, which bring moist air from the south-west and west, are the main cause for mudflow events in the study area.

the occurrence of mudflow events is mainly controlled by the synoptic scale atmospheric processes, which are responsible for moisture advection from the Mediterranean and central Europe to Uzbekistan.
the mudflow events in the study area are mainly triggered by the synoptic scale weather systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mudflow occurrences in Central Asia are mainly influenced by the synoptic scale atmospheric processes.
the CWTs are the most important synoptic weather types that influence the mudflow occurrence in the study area.
the CWTs W, SW and NW are the main atmospheric regimes, which are associated with the occurrence of mudflows in the piedmont regions of Uzbekistan.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synoptic weather type approach is useful for identifying the atmospheric regimes that are responsible for triggering of mudflow occurrences.
the mudflow occurrences in Central Asia and Uzbekistan are mainly driven by synoptic weather patterns.
synoptic weather types are important drivers of mudflow occurrences.
